calls.head: Picky against trigger-happy
calls.body: On shot quality, St. Louis is one of the league’s best, but Chicago is near the bottom. The more dangerous chances should be the Blues’.
calls.call: The Blues’ shots are more dangerous on average than the Blackhawks’.

calls.title: St. Louis got the better looks
calls.plain: The Blues came out clearly ahead on shot quality, as the gap between these two suggested.
calls.said: the Blues would get better looks than the Blackhawks
calls.beyond: Chicago usually gets worse looks than most teams, and St. Louis usually allows fewer dangerous shots than most teams. Even by those standards, this was a night of harmless shots: Chicago’s shots at 5-on-5 had a 3.7% chance of scoring on the average shot, against their usual 6.1% (about 5.9% against St. Louis) and a league average of 6.3%. A team strays this far about once every 30 games.

calls.head: Where the Blues have the edge: forecheck pressure
calls.body: The Blues are around the middle of the league for forecheck pressure, and the Blackhawks are one of the worst. It’s the widest gap between these two, though not a huge one.
calls.call: The Blues put more forecheck pressure on than the Blackhawks.

CHI.head: We had Chicago as slight underdogs (41%), and they pulled it off.

STL.head: We leaned St. Louis’s way (59%), but Chicago had other ideas.

surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: The Blackhawks handle the Blues
paras: Mason McTavish opened the scoring for the Blues late in the first. St. Louis had a goal taken off for offside early in the second. Sam Rinzel and Anton Frondell scored 2:00 apart early in the second to turn a 1-0 deficit into a 2-1 lead. Cole Smith scored his first goal for Chicago with 1:09 left into the empty net with 1:09 left. Connor McMichael scored his first goal for St. Louis on the power play with 39 seconds left to pull the Blues within one with the goalie pulled. Frank Nazar added the empty-netter with 4 seconds left to make it 4-2.

The Blues had a little more of the play. The Blackhawks had the finish. Spencer Knight made 25 saves for the Hawks, and Joel Hofer stopped 17 of 19. The Blackhawks improved to 1-3-0, and the Blues fell to 1-2-0.

items.text: The Blackhawks won for the first time this season, in their fourth game.
The Blackhawks won their home opener.
Both of the preview’s calls held.
